entities.summary:
Princeton University, founded in 1746 as the College of New Jersey, is one of America's oldest and most prestigious research universities, located in Princeton, New Jersey. With an undergraduate enrollment of only 5,500 students — among the smallest in the Ivy League — Princeton has produced 69 Nobel laureates, 2 US presidents (James Madison and Woodrow Wilson), and maintains the world's highest faculty-to-student ratio among major research universities.

Princeton was founded by New Light Presbyterians seeking an alternative to Harvard's Congregationalism, and was the scene of a pivotal Revolutionary War battle in 1777 when George Washington defeated British forces at the Battle of Princeton. The university's Nassau Hall (1756) served briefly as the US Capitol in 1783 when Congress met there, and was the site where the Continental Congress learned of the peace treaty with Britain.

Princeton's Graduate School, Institute for Advanced Study (associated with but independent of Princeton), and Woodrow Wilson School of Public and International Affairs have made it a center for mathematics, physics, and political science. Albert Einstein spent his later career at the Institute for Advanced Study, working in Princeton from 1933 until his death in 1955. John Nash (A Beautiful Mind), Alan Turing, and Kurt Gödel were also associated with Princeton's mathematical tradition. Princeton's residential college system and eating clubs create a distinctive social culture.
